text: Parse endpoint converts documents into structured JSON with text, tables, figures, layout, and formatting
quote: Parse is Reducto’s foundational endpoint. It converts documents into structured JSON with text, tables, figures, layout, and formatting

text: Extract pulls specific fields into structured JSON matching a user-defined schema
quote: Extract pulls specific fields from documents as structured JSON. You define a schema describing the data you need, and Reducto returns values matching that schema

text: Split identifies which pages contain naturally-described sections and returns page ranges
quote: Split identifies which pages contain which sections of a document. You describe sections in natural language, and Reducto returns the page numbers where each section lives.

text: Route/classify documents into categories defined in natural language before processing
quote: Route documents by type before processing. Define categories in natural language.

text: Fill PDF forms and modify DOCX files programmatically via natural-language instructions
quote: Fill PDF forms and modify DOCX files programmatically with natural language instructions.

text: Chain classification, parsing, extraction, and editing into a single multi-step workflow call
quote: Multi-step workflows that chain classification, parsing, extraction, and editing into single API calls

text: Official CLI provides terminal access to parse, extract, split, classify, and edit operations
quote: The Reducto CLI gives you direct terminal access to Reducto’s document capabilities: parse, extract, split, classify, and edit.

text: Official MCP integration lets agents in Claude, Cursor, VS Code, etc. classify, parse, extract, split, and edit documents as part of their reasoning loop
quote: Once installed, agents in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, or any other Model Context Protocol client can classify, parse, extract, split, and edit documents

text: Async run_job() call kicks off processing and returns a job ID for status polling
quote: `run_job()` Calls async endpoint, returns job ID

text: Webhooks (via Svix) provide cryptographic signing, automatic retries with backoff, and a delivery dashboard
quote: Svix webhooks provide cryptographic request signing, automatic retries with exponential backoff, and a delivery dashboard for debugging.

text: Citations feature returns bounding-box coordinates tying each extracted field to its source text
quote: Citations tell you exactly where each extracted value came from in the document. When enabled, every field includes bounding box coordinates pointing to the source text.

text: Configurable chunking (chunk_mode/chunk_size) controls RAG-oriented segmentation of parsed output
Per-scope 'agentic' config lets you set custom prompts or enable advanced chart extraction
quote: Add an entry to the `agentic` array for each scope that needs customized processing. Each entry must include a custom prompt or enable advanced chart extraction.

text: Tables are extracted and returnable in several structured formats
quote: Reducto extracts tables from documents and can return them in several formats.

text: All customer data/storage stays inside the customer's VPC while processing runs on Reducto's dedicated GPUs
quote: All data and storage reside in the customer’s VPC, while ephemeral processing is handled by Reducto’s dedicated GPU infrastructure.

text: Large files over 100MB (up to 5GB) can be uploaded via a presigned URL method
quote: Files over 100MB? Use the presigned URL method which supports files up to 5GB.

text: Python SDK exposes client.parse.run() for direct document parsing via URL or file ID
quote: result = client.parse.run(input="https://cdn.reducto.ai/samples/fidelity-example.pdf")

text: Batch-queued Parse/Extract jobs receive a 20% usage discount for high-volume processing
quote: Parse and Extract jobs submitted through the batch queue receive a 20% usage discount.
